sentences.text: Juratyrant langhami is the only known species within the genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur that lived in England during the late Jurassic period.
The animal is known from a single partial skeleton that includes a complete pelvis, parts of the legs, and vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail.
This creature is classified within the superfamily Tyrannosauroidea and the family Stokesosauridae.
Scientists have estimated its weight ranging from 300 kg to as much as 648 kg, showing significant variation in reconstruction.
One estimate suggests the dinosaur was 5 meters long.
The holotype specimen, which is the specific fossil the species is based on, was discovered in Dorset, England, in 1984 by the fossil collector Peter Langham.

Although mentioned in earlier papers, the species was not formally described until 2008 when Roger Benson assigned it to Stokesosaurus; it was later reclassified into its own genus, Juratyrant, by Benson and Stephen Brusatte in 2013.
The fossil was found in Kimmeridge Clay strata belonging to the Pectinatites pectinatus ammonite zone.
There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of this dinosaur.
Juratyrant langhami lived approximately 150 million years ago in what is now Europe during the late Jurassic Tithonian stage.
Other sources place its existence between 145.06 and 143.1 million years ago.
A 2013 study by Loewen et al. suggested Juratyrant belonged to Proceratosauridae based on a shared narrow preacetabular notch.
However, a 2016 analysis by Brusatte and Carr placed Juratyrant as a tyrannosauroid slightly more advanced than Proceratosauridae and Dilong.
More recently, a 2025 study by Delcourt et al. found that equal-weight phylogenetic analyses placed Juratyrant as an ancestral megaraptoran, which would make it the oldest known record of that group.
